The gate as a checklist, not a judgement: every AC discharged, every CI gate green. rfc-check, req-registry --check, doc-drift, req-status, control-plane-check, spec-discipline, anti-pattern-gate. Read every exit code DIRECTLY — 'cmd | tail; echo $?' reports tail's status, an error that reached a PR description here and needed a public correction.

The anchor cannot pass a stage gate yet, and the blocker is measured. CI here triggers only on push to main and on pull_request, so anchor/implementation has NEVER been gated - no PR exists for it. Running the cheap gates locally on the anchor worktree at 62750676 with python3.12: doc-drift exits 1 with 25 CURRENT and 35 DRIFT. The drift is the anchor doing its job - it migrated the five front-end files plus the corpus, and 35 design docs pin content digests over governed files that moved. Separately, and this is the handoff 90 .md item made exact: 90 of 145 tracked .md files repo-wide carry a v2 clause keyword as a word, 63 of the 78 under .design/. The two sets overlap but are not the same problem - 28 of the 35 drifted docs ALSO carry v2 prose, 7 drift only. So re-pinning all 35 mechanically would certify 28 documents that still describe a surface the anchor removed, which is a pin asserting something false rather than a chore. Correction to a number I reported minutes earlier in this session: I first measured 0 of 78 design docs carrying v2 keywords, which was a false negative - git grep -E does not honour \\b, so the pattern matched nothing and read as clean. Caught by a control search for requires, which returned 51 files where 0 was impossible. Same rule as the zsh :t and PIPESTATUS cases already recorded: a search that can report clean by matching nothing needs a control that must match.

The doc migration is done and pushed as c072135a on anchor/implementation, a separate commit on top of 62750676. 97 files - 86 md and 11 th - 1792 insertions and 1792 deletions, 2296 clause-spelling replacements plus 26 clause lists reordered and 2 sentences rewritten by hand. doc-drift now exits 0 on the anchor, down from 35 DRIFT. Five populations deliberately NOT migrated, each for a stated reason: .design/rfcs/ because an RFC quotes the surface it changes, thermite2-semantics.md because it self-describes as the normative home for the SHIPPED Stage-1 semantics, CHANGELOG.md as a historical record, .crosslink/rules/ where req is an Express request object in other-language rule files, and .claude/agents/ as upstream harness config. Two findings a rename cannot handle. First, the AST field names STAY v2 - Contract { req: Clause, ens: Vec<Clause>, fx: EffectRow } - because RFC-6 deliberately left the Rust surface alone, so about 30 doc sites like Contract.fx and fx: EffectRow are correct identifiers and were protected from the rewrite rather than renamed. That leaves a permanent vocabulary split: the surface says requires while the AST says req. Second, RFC-6 changed clause ORDER as well as spelling, so a pure rename produces text that is spelling-correct and order-wrong; 26 lists were reordered to !/requires/ensures.

The anchor is under CI for the first time, as PR 13 in staging, base rfc/full-words so the diff is the implementation alone rather than the process layer. Two commits were needed beyond the doc migration. cargo fmt --all --check failed on the anchor and the fault is ours - the base d042c17c exits 0 - because requires/ensures/! are longer than req/ens/fx and pushed call sites past the width, mostly parse_program test fixtures. 32 files reformatted, verified as layout-only by comparing each file with all whitespace stripped: 17 byte-identical, the other 15 differing only by rustfmt adding a trailing comma inside a wrapped call. That reformatting then moved 22 design-doc pins, the same consequence this branch already met once, and each was re-pinned with a note naming THIS cause - rustfmt, not the surface change - so a reader can tell it apart from the surface re-pins in c072135a. Branch is 57feaf9d. Locally cargo fmt, doc-drift, req-status, control-plane-check and rfc-check each exit 0, and cargo check --workspace --all-targets exits 0. What CI has still never run here is everything past the cheap gates: clippy, the bv gate, doctests, skill-budget, and crucially g3 and g4, the actual stage gates, which need Verus, Lean with mathlib and CaDiCaL that this machine does not have.

GATE-RESULT: the anchor passes. PR 13 at 66969f10 is 13 of 13 green in staging - checks, g3, g4, kernel-image, lean-probe, four lean-spine-forge shards and four test shards. This is the first time ANY stage gate has run on anchor/implementation: CI triggers only on pull_request and on push to main, and no PR existed for the branch until today. Verified substantively rather than by the aggregate tick: the g4 job ran 15m52s with real elan, Mathlib cache, Z3, and pinned CaDiCaL and drat-trim installs, and its log ends test result: ok. 28 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 497 filtered out; finished in 160.56s, then G4 gate passed. g3 passed on the previous run too. Getting here took four commits past the migration itself, each with its own cause: c072135a migrating 90 design docs and re-pinning 35, 57feaf9d reformatting what the rename lengthened and re-pinning 22, and 66969f10 migrating the REQ registry labels and regenerating the status view after the doc pass had hand-edited a GENERATED region. Every one of those was invisible until a gate ran, which is the argument for putting the branch under CI before reasoning about whether it was ready.
